passages.heading: Tapas
passages.text: Niyama. Voluntary intensity that burns through samskara.

passages.heading: Default Mode Network
passages.text: DMN: mPFC + posterior cingulate + angular gyrus. Hyperactive in depression and rumination. Quietens in meditation (Brewer et al., 2011).

passages.heading: Amygdala
passages.text: Almond-shaped subcortical structure. Triggers fight/flight before conscious appraisal. Reduces volume after 8 weeks of MBSR (Hölzel et al., 2011).

passages.heading: Prefrontal Cortex
passages.text: Last brain region to fully develop (~25). Thickens with sustained meditation practice.

passages.heading: Polyvagal
passages.text: Stephen Porges. Maps three states: ventral vagal (safe), sympathetic (fight/flight), dorsal vagal (freeze/collapse). Foundational for trauma-informed practice.

passages.heading: Interoception
passages.text: The 8th sense. Anchored in insula. Increases measurably with body-based contemplative practice.

passages.heading: Neuroplasticity
passages.text: What practice changes. Not metaphor: synaptic density, cortical thickness, white-matter tracts all measurably shift.

passages.heading: HRV
passages.text: Beat-to-beat variation. Higher = better regulation, recovery, emotional range. Rises with breath practice.

passages.heading: Cortisol
passages.text: Chronic elevation = inflammation, insomnia, weight gain, accelerated aging. Drops with regular meditation.

passages.heading: Dopamine
passages.text: Not 'pleasure' — wanting. Chronic over-firing (notifications, scroll) creates tolerance and anhedonia.

passages.heading: BDNF
passages.text: Increases with exercise, meditation, fasting. Foundation of adult neuroplasticity.

passages.heading: Rumination
passages.text: Strongest single predictor of depression onset. Differs from problem-solving — produces no resolution.

passages.heading: Spiritual Bypass
passages.text: Term coined by John Welwood, 1984. The shadow side of premature transcendence.

passages.heading: Dark Night
passages.text: St John of the Cross. Maps to certain meditation jhanas and to depressive episodes in advanced practitioners (Willoughby Britton, Varieties of Contemplative Experience).

passages.heading: Locus of Control
passages.text: Internal locus predicts higher resilience, agency, mental health.

passages.heading: Allostatic Load
passages.text: McEwen, 1993. The body's bill for sustained dysregulation.

passages.heading: Vipassana
passages.text: Theravada Buddhist practice. Goenka's 10-day silent retreat is the modern flagship.

passages.heading: Yoga Nidra
passages.text: Systematic body-scan + intention. 20 min = ~2 hours of sleep in restorative effect.

passages.text: Bhakti practice. Activates limbic system and bonds group nervous systems.

passages.heading: Mauna

passages.heading: Pratyahara
passages.text: Fifth limb of Raja Yoga. Foundation for concentration.

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: Compiled the 196 sutras as a transmission, not a treatise. Eight limbs as scaffolding for any seeker.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Yogaś citta-vṛtti-nirodhaḥ. — Yoga Sutra 1.2

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: On the battlefield, Arjuna froze. Krishna didn't say 'don't fight' — he said 'fight without attachment.' That changed everything.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: You have a right to action alone, never to its fruits. — Bhagavad Gita 2.47

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: A prince who saw old age, sickness, death. Sat under a tree until he saw clearly.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: All conditioned things are impermanent. — Dhammapada 277

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: At 16, a sudden death-experience showed him directly: the body dies, awareness doesn't. He left for Arunachala and never lectured a day.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Your duty is to BE; and not to be this or that. — Be As You Are

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: A small Bombay shopkeeper who rolled beedis. His teaching was relentless. 'I Am That' is a knife.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Wisdom is knowing I am nothing, love is knowing I am everything. — I Am That

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: A Rajput princess who refused to be a queen because her husband was Krishna. Drank poison, sang it into nectar.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: I have given my heart to the One who does not break. — Mira bhajan

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: A scholar until Shams arrived. Then he became a poet of fire.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Out beyond ideas of wrongdoing and rightdoing, there is a field. I will meet you there. — Masnavi

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: Came west in 1920 with a single instruction: bring kriya to the modern householder.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Be calmly active and actively calm. — Autobiography of a Yogi

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: Brought Vedanta to Chicago in 1893. Did the work. Died at 39, having ignited a civilizational current.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Strength is life, weakness is death. — Complete Works

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: A temple priest who took every path — Christian, Muslim, tantric — to verify directly. Each one delivered.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: As many faiths, so many paths. — Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: Polymath of Kashmir. Tantraloka is one of the most complete maps of consciousness ever written.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Wherever the mind goes, there is the state of Shiva. — Vijnana Bhairava 116

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: Walked India four times before age 32. Set up four mathas. Reframed Hindu thought single-handedly.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Brahma satyam jagan mithya, jivo brahmaiva naparah. — Vivekachudamani

passages.heading: Story
passages.text: Self-taught. Self-initiated. Lived in continuous bliss without any path. The exception that humbles every path.

passages.heading: Sutra
passages.text: Whatever exists exists in essence as Existence itself. — Words of Sri Anandamayi Ma

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Refreshing notifications. Re-reading sent messages. Mood that rises and falls with likes, replies, the absence of replies.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: Practice: do one good thing and tell no one. Do it again tomorrow.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: The task you've moved across 4 to-do lists. Opening 8 tabs to escape the one that matters.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: Two-minute rule: open the document. Don't write. Just open it. Daily.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Re-writing the same email 12 times. Micromanaging others. Body tight before any uncertainty.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: Practice: hand over one decision per week to someone else. Don't review.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Always 'on'. Exhausted by small talk. Resume-thinking even during rest.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: 10 unproductive minutes daily, scheduled. Stare. Wander. Don't justify.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Other people's lives feel sharper than yours. Scrolling = subtle ache.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: 30-day fast from one comparison surface. Notice what fills the silence.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: The same conversation, replayed at 11:47 PM, with better comebacks each time.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: Body-first: when rumination starts, walk 10 minutes. Don't think. Walk.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Quoting Rumi instead of feeling. 'It's all one' when something specific is hurting.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: When you reach for a teaching, ask: what am I trying to not feel?

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Money, time, love — never enough. Hoarding. Bracing for loss.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: Daily: name 3 things present. Specific. Concrete. Out loud.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Always the helper. Tired but can't say no. Identity built on being needed.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: Say no once this week, without explanation. Survive it.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Life happens to you. Patterns repeat. Story of being wronged is well-rehearsed.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: Daily: one small thing fully chosen, not endured.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Substance, scroll, sugar, sex — the thing that promises peace and delivers more wanting.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: 30-day fast from the one. Feel what shows up. That's the actual practice.

passages.heading: Feels like
passages.text: Nothing ships. Standard moves whenever you approach it. Self-criticism dressed as standards.

passages.heading: Way out
passages.text: Ship one thing this week at 70%. Watch what does and doesn't happen.

passages.heading: Origin
passages.text: Bhagavad Gita, chapters 2–6. Lived by Krishna, Janaka, Gandhi.

passages.heading: For whom
passages.text: Gut-dominant doers. People whose nervous system needs to move. Founders, parents, builders.

passages.heading: Origin
passages.text: Narada Bhakti Sutras. Lived by Mirabai, Chaitanya, Ramakrishna, Rumi.

passages.heading: For whom
passages.text: Heart-dominant. People who cry easily, who need a 'You' to talk to, who are moved by music.

passages.heading: Origin
passages.text: Upanishads, Ashtavakra Gita, Ribhu Gita. Lived by Ramana Maharshi, Nisargadatta, Shankara.

passages.heading: For whom
passages.text: Head-dominant. People who must understand. Engineers, philosophers, the relentlessly logical.
